entradas.text: “I will hold my own umbrella.”
entradas.menu: “I will hold my own umbrella.”

entradas.text: It was raining as my car came to a stop by the Holsord Grand Cemetery.
He offered to carry my umbrella.
I let him carry my umbrella.
entradas.menu: Let him carry your umbrella.

entradas.text: Under the watchful eyes of security officers, I started walking amidst the gravestones.
A small crowd of family and friends gathered around the final resting place of Serge Wolkner.
Some in the media were calling him a hero: the brave driver who saved the president by sacrificing his life. It was true.
I walked up to his widow, Suzan. I had never met her in person before.
Little Anton was crying silently next to his sister, Erica.
Little Georg was crying silently next to his sister, Erica.
They were too young to experience the pain of losing a father.
I walked over to stand next to the priest, who stepped back upon my arrival.
“Today, we are mourning a hero of our nation.”
entradas.menu: “Today, we are mourning a hero of our nation.”

entradas.text: I looked around at everyone's faces.
Despite my protests, security wouldn't permit a larger funeral.
“Today, we are gathered here to mourn the man who saved my life.”
entradas.menu: “Today, we have gathered here to mourn the man who saved my life.”

entradas.text: “Today, we are sending off a friend, a husband and a father.”
entradas.menu: “Today, we are sending off a friend, a husband and a father.”

entradas.text: “Serge Wolkner was a true Sord. He was honest, proud and brave.”
entradas.menu: “Serge Wolkner was a true Sord. He was honest, proud and brave.”

entradas.text: “Serge Wolkner was more than a simple driver for me. He was a real friend.”
entradas.menu: “Serge Wolkner was more than a simple driver for me. He was a real friend.”

entradas.text: “Serge Wolkner was loved by many and he will be missed dearly.”
entradas.menu: “Serge Wolkner was loved by many and he will be missed dearly.”

entradas.text: “I will always cherish the moments I spent with him.”
entradas.menu: “I will always cherish the moments I spent with him.”

entradas.text: “He has left us too soon.”
entradas.menu: “He has left us too soon.”

entradas.text: “His memory is engraved in our minds and hearts. We must remember him well.”
entradas.menu: “His memory is engraved in all of our minds and hearts. We must remember him well.”

entradas.text: “I wouldn't be able to find a single person who did not enjoy his company.”
entradas.menu: “I wouldn't be able to find a single person who did not enjoy his company.”

entradas.text: “I will never forget that I am standing here right now because of his sacrifice.”
entradas.menu: “I will never forget that I am standing here right now because of his sacrifice.”

entradas.text: “I will be forever burdened with the fact that this happened because of me.”
entradas.menu: “I will be forever burdened with the fact that this happened because of me.”

entradas.text: “I am granting him the title, 'Hero of Sordland'.”
entradas.menu: “I am granting him the title, 'Hero of Sordland'.”

entradas.text: “I swear to cherish the life he has once again granted me with.”
entradas.menu: “I swear to cherish the life he has once again granted me with.”

entradas.text: “His death will be avenged. This, I promise.”
entradas.menu: “His death will be avenged. This, I promise.”

entradas.text: “The family he has left behind will have the full support of the government.”
entradas.menu: “The family he has left behind will have the full support of the government.”

entradas.text: “I am granting him the military rank of Major.”
entradas.menu: “I am granting him the military rank of Major.”

entradas.text: “In these dark times, we need to come together in unity.”
entradas.menu: “In these dark times, we need to come together in unity.”

entradas.text: “Farewell, brother.”
entradas.menu: “Farewell, brother.”

entradas.text: “Thank you for your service, Serge.”
entradas.menu: “Thank you for your service, Serge.”

entradas.text: “May his memory last forever.”
entradas.menu: “May his memory last forever.”

entradas.text: The casket started to be lowered.
I put my hand in my pocket and pulled out the watch Serge once gave me.
I recalled that he said it protected his father from the evil of this world.
At first I didn't believe it, but now I did.
I kept the watch and put it back in my pocket.
entradas.menu: Keep the watch.

entradas.text: I walked over to Serge's son and gave him the watch.
entradas.menu: Give the watch to Serge's son.

entradas.text: I placed the watch on Serge's grave.
entradas.menu: Place the watch on his grave.

entradas.text: As the casket hit the ground, mourners sprinkled handfuls of dirt on Serge's grave.
His wife and children hugged each other.
I realized it was time for me to leave.
It started pouring.
I wiped their tears.
entradas.menu: Wipe their tears.

entradas.text: I patted them on their heads.
entradas.menu: Pat them on their heads.

entradas.text: I gave them a hug.
entradas.menu: Give them a hug.

entradas.text: “Your father was a great man. Don't ever forget that.”
entradas.menu: “Your father was a great man. Don't ever forget that.”

entradas.text: “It's okay to cry. Let it all out.”
entradas.menu: “It's okay to cry. Let it all out.”

entradas.text: “Ms. Wolkner. I will never forget your husband's service and his heroic sacrifice."
entradas.menu: “Ms. Wolkner. I will never forget your husband's service and his heroic sacrifice."

entradas.text: “I am so sorry, Suzan.”
entradas.menu: “I am so sorry, Suzan.”

entradas.text: “My condolences.”
entradas.menu: “My condolences.”

entradas.text: We hugged and she cried on my shoulder. I crouched next to Serge's children.
“You must be strong.”
entradas.menu: “You must be strong.”

entradas.text: As I turned my back on Serge's final resting place, I looked up at the dark clouds above.
My new driver opened the door. I had forgotten his name already.
I was losing track of how many funerals I had attended by now.
Under the watchful eyes of security officers in military uniforms, I started walking amidst the gravestones.
She was wearing an elegant black dress and a beautiful diamond necklace. She thanked me for everything I'd done for her family.
She was wearing a simple but well-fitting black dress and holding a portrait of Serge in her arms. She thanked me for everything I'd done for her children.
She was wearing a simple but well-fitting black dress and holding a portrait of Serge in her arms.
"Don't worry. I'll make sure you and your children are still well cared for."
"I wish I could have done more. He deserved it."
"Don't worry. I'll make sure the children are still well cared for."
